title: First Word All Beings Say Bismillah Through The Language Of Their State

questions.question: What question is raised at the start of the passage about all created things?
questions.answer: It asks whether all beings, in their own created way, say “In the Name of Allah.”

questions.question: What example is given to show that one person cannot force a whole town by his own power alone?
questions.answer: The example is of a man driving the people of a town and making them work, which shows he must be acting with official authority and support.

questions.question: In that example, what does the person’s success prove about him?
questions.answer: It proves that he is not acting by himself but under a ruler’s command and strength.

questions.question: How is that town example connected to the rest of creation?
questions.answer: It is used as a comparison to show that created things also work by Allah’s power, not by themselves.

questions.question: What do seeds and grains show about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: They show that tiny things can carry the beginning of huge trees, which points to power far greater than their own size.

questions.question: What lesson do trees teach in this passage?
questions.answer: They show that they receive their provisions from Allah’s mercy and then bring fruits and benefits to people.

questions.question: How are gardens described, and what does that description mean?
questions.answer: They are described like cooking places full of many foods, meaning Allah prepares many kinds of provision through them.

questions.question: Which animals are mentioned, and what do they provide?
questions.answer: Cows, camels, sheep, and goats are mentioned, and they provide milk.

questions.question: Why is milk presented as a sign of mercy in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it is a pure, gentle, nourishing food given through animals for human benefit.

questions.question: What surprising work do roots and rootlets do?
questions.answer: They move through hard ground and rock even though they are soft and delicate.

questions.question: What main point is made by saying everything becomes obedient when Allah’s name is mentioned?
questions.answer: The point is that created things submit to Allah’s command.

questions.question: How do the roots answer people who explain everything only by nature?
questions.answer: They show that hardness and physical barriers are not independent, because even soft roots can pass through them by Allah’s command.

questions.question: What two things are especially challenged in the passage as not having final control?
questions.answer: Heat and hardness are shown not to have final control.

questions.question: Why are Prophets Musa and Ibrahim, peace be upon them, mentioned here?
questions.answer: They are mentioned as examples to show that Allah can make hard things split and harmful heat lose its harm.

questions.question: What do the leaves show by staying fresh in strong heat?
questions.answer: They show that even delicate things survive by Allah’s command and care, not by their own power.

questions.question: What claim from earlier is confirmed at the beginning of this passage?
questions.answer: The claim that all beings say “In the Name of Allah” through their condition and actions.

questions.question: Why would a person who controls a whole town not be seen as acting alone?
questions.answer: Because one person does not have enough power by himself to do that, so he must be backed by higher authority.

questions.question: What does the image of a soldier help the reader understand?
questions.answer: It helps the reader understand how someone can act with power that comes from a ruler rather than from himself.

questions.question: According to the comparison, how do created things act?
questions.answer: They act with the power and permission of Almighty Allah.

questions.question: Why are seeds and grains important examples in this passage?
questions.answer: Because they are very small, yet they become the start of large trees, which shows amazing divine power.

questions.question: What do trees do for people after receiving from Allah’s mercy?
questions.answer: They present fruits and other benefits to people.

questions.question: How are gardens pictured in a way that helps us understand divine provision?
questions.answer: They are pictured as places where many different foods are prepared and served.

questions.question: What does the variety of foods in gardens suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests wide, rich, and carefully arranged mercy from Allah.

questions.question: What common farm animals are used as signs in the passage?
questions.answer: Cows, camels, sheep, and goats.

questions.question: What do these animals produce, and why is that meaningful?
questions.answer: They produce milk, which is meaningful because it is pure and beneficial and comes as a mercy from Allah.

questions.question: What contrast is made between the softness of roots and the hardness of the earth?
questions.answer: The roots are very soft, but they still pass through hard ground and rock.

questions.question: What does that contrast teach about cause and effect in the world?
questions.answer: It teaches that the real cause is Allah’s command, not just material strength.

questions.question: How does the passage respond to people who trust only in physical laws like heat and hardness?
questions.answer: It says those things are also under command and are not independent powers.

questions.question: What is the purpose of referring to the miracle of Musa, peace be upon him?
questions.answer: It helps explain that Allah can make rock open despite its hardness.

questions.question: What is the purpose of referring to the story of Ibrahim, peace be upon him?
questions.answer: It helps explain that Allah can make heat harmless.

questions.question: What overall message do roots and leaves together give?
questions.answer: They show that both strong barriers and harsh conditions are under Allah’s control.

questions.question: At the opening of the passage, what issue is being asked and answered?
questions.answer: Whether all beings truly declare Allah’s name through the way they are made and the way they act.

questions.question: What scene is used first to help explain the answer?
questions.answer: A scene where one person forces the people of a town to gather and work.

questions.question: What conclusion would a careful observer make from that scene?
questions.answer: That the person must be acting with a ruler’s support and authority.

questions.question: Why is this comparison effective for understanding the natural world?
questions.answer: Because it shows that great results point to a greater power behind them.

questions.question: How do tiny seeds point to something beyond themselves?
questions.answer: They contain the beginning of huge trees, which shows they are working through Allah’s power.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the work of trees?
questions.answer: They receive gifts from Allah’s mercy and then pass those gifts on to people.

questions.question: In what way are gardens more than just places where plants grow?
questions.answer: They are shown as places where many kinds of nourishment are prepared.

questions.question: What does the garden image teach us about Allah?
questions.answer: It teaches that Allah provides many different blessings with wisdom and care.

questions.question: Why are milk-giving animals called blessed in this passage?
questions.answer: Because they provide a clean and valuable food as a mercy from Allah.

questions.question: What makes the work of roots especially amazing?
questions.answer: Their softness makes it surprising that they can penetrate hard earth and rock.

questions.question: What happens to things when Allah’s name and mercy are mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: They become obedient and manageable under His command.

questions.question: Who is criticized in this passage, and for what mistake?
questions.answer: Those who explain everything by nature alone are criticized for ignoring Allah’s rule over creation.

questions.question: How do the roots answer that mistake without speaking words?
questions.answer: Their actions show that hard matter cannot resist Allah’s command.

questions.question: What do the leaves show by staying moist in severe heat?
questions.answer: They show that heat does not act independently and that Allah preserves what He wills.

questions.question: What is the main lesson of the examples of seeds, trees, gardens, animals, roots, and leaves taken together?
questions.answer: All of them show that creation works in Allah’s name and by His power, mercy, and command.

questions.question: What statement about all beings is examined at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: The statement that all beings say “In the Name of Allah” through their natural state.

questions.question: What human example is given to support that statement?
questions.answer: A single person moving and controlling a whole town by force.

questions.question: What would show that this person had official backing?
questions.answer: His ability to command many people successfully would show he was supported by higher power.

questions.question: How does this human example prepare us to think about nature?
questions.answer: It teaches us that great actions in the world must also come from a greater authority.

questions.question: What do grains and seeds carry that seems far beyond their own size?
questions.answer: They carry the beginning and burden of large trees.

questions.question: What does that teach about their own power?
questions.answer: It teaches that their own power is not enough, so they act by Allah’s power.

questions.question: What role do trees have after taking from divine mercy?
questions.answer: They present food and benefits to human beings.

questions.question: Why are gardens compared to places where food is cooked?
questions.answer: Because they produce many different kinds of nourishment as if they were preparing meals.

questions.question: What is special about the milk from the animals named in the passage?
questions.answer: It is pure, beneficial, and generously provided through Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: Which animals are listed as examples of this mercy?
questions.answer: Cows, camels, sheep, and goats.

questions.question: What is surprising about roots and rootlets?
questions.answer: They are soft and fine, yet they pass through hard materials.

questions.question: What does their success show about the earth and rocks they enter?
questions.answer: It shows those hard things are also under Allah’s command.

questions.question: What false idea is being corrected when the passage speaks against trust in heat and hardness?
questions.answer: The false idea that physical forces act on their own without Allah.

questions.question: How does the example connected to Musa, peace be upon him, strengthen the argument?
questions.answer: It reminds the reader that Allah can make solid rock open.

questions.question: How does the example connected to Ibrahim, peace be upon him, strengthen the argument?
questions.answer: It reminds the reader that Allah can make burning heat lose its harm.

questions.question: What big truth should a student understand from the final examples in the passage?
questions.answer: Even the strongest natural forces obey Allah, and delicate things succeed by His will.

questions.question: What is the short question asked at the start of this passage section?
questions.answer: It asks if it is really true that all beings say “In the Name of Allah” through their condition.

questions.question: What answer is given to that question?
questions.answer: A strong confirmation is given that it is true.

questions.question: What kind of example is used first to prove it?
questions.answer: An example from human society about a person controlling a whole town.

questions.question: Why can’t that person’s action be explained as personal strength only?
questions.answer: Because the task is too great for one person acting alone.

questions.question: If he is not acting by his own strength, whose support must he have?
questions.answer: He must have the backing of a ruler and government.

questions.question: How does the passage apply this idea to everything in creation?
questions.answer: It says all things act in Allah’s name and by His power.

questions.question: What do small seeds teach us when they grow into large trees?
questions.answer: They teach us that great results can come from tiny things only through Allah’s command.

questions.question: What do trees seem to do after receiving provision from mercy?
questions.answer: They hand out blessings and food to people.

questions.question: How are gardens described in a way that highlights abundance?
questions.answer: They are described like places where many kinds of foods are prepared together.

questions.question: What gift do animals such as cows and sheep provide?
questions.answer: They provide milk.

questions.question: Why is that gift important in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it is shown as a clean and life-giving mercy from Allah.

questions.question: What makes the movement of roots through rock so meaningful?
questions.answer: Their softness makes it clear that their success does not come from brute force.

questions.question: According to the passage, what happens when Allah’s mercy and name are involved?
questions.answer: Things become obedient and barriers are overcome.

questions.question: How does the passage challenge a view that depends only on nature?
questions.answer: It shows examples where material explanations alone are not enough.

questions.question: What do the leaves prove by staying fresh in intense heat?
questions.answer: They prove that heat is not the ultimate ruler and that Allah protects what He wills.

questions.question: What is one central message of the whole passage?
questions.answer: The whole world shows Allah’s power and mercy through the way created things work.

questions.question: What belief about creation is brought up again at the beginning of this passage?
questions.answer: The belief that all beings, by their state and actions, declare Allah’s name.

questions.question: What simple real-life comparison is used to explain this idea?
questions.answer: A comparison about one man forcing the people of a town to gather and labor.

questions.question: What would a person naturally understand from seeing that event?
questions.answer: He would understand that the man had authority from above and was not working independently.

questions.question: What larger truth does that comparison point to?
questions.answer: It points to the truth that created things also work under divine authority.

questions.question: Why are seeds and grains strong evidence in this argument?
questions.answer: Because very tiny things begin the growth of massive trees.

questions.question: What do trees give to people, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They give fruits and other provisions that come from Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: What picture is used for gardens, and what does it show?
questions.answer: Gardens are pictured like cooking pots or kitchens, showing rich and varied provision.

questions.question: What does the passage say about certain domestic animals?
questions.answer: It says they bring forth milk as a mercy and nourishment for people.

questions.question: Which animals are named to make this point clear?
questions.answer: Cows, camels, sheep, and goats.

questions.question: How are roots described, and why is that important?
questions.answer: They are described as very soft and fine, which makes their power to pass through rock seem amazing.

questions.question: What does their ability to pass through hard places teach about the world?
questions.answer: It teaches that the world obeys Allah’s command.

questions.question: What happens to the idea that nature acts by itself when we look at these examples?
questions.answer: That idea becomes weak, because the examples point beyond nature to Allah’s will.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention hard rock in connection with Prophet Musa, peace be upon him?
questions.answer: To show that Allah can make even solid rock break open.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention fire in connection with Prophet Ibrahim, peace be upon him?
questions.answer: To show that Allah can make heat stop harming.

questions.question: What do both the roots and the leaves have in common as signs?
questions.answer: Both show that delicate created things can do remarkable things by Allah’s command.

questions.question: If a student had to summarize this passage in one sentence, what would be a good summary?
questions.answer: Everything in creation works by Allah’s power and mercy, not by its own independent strength.
